learn.title: Repeated multiplication
learn.body: An exponent is a short way to write repeated multiplication. $2^3$ means $2\times 2\times 2=8$. The number being multiplied (2) is the base. The small raised number (3) is the exponent. We say "2 to the power of 3".

learn.title: Squares and cubes
learn.body: An exponent of 2 is called squared, and 3 is called cubed. $5^2=25$ and $4^3=64$. Be careful: $2^3$ is not $2\times 3$. It is $2\times 2\times 2$. Learn the squares up to $12^2=144$; you will use them often.

learn.title: Powers of 10 and zero
learn.body: Powers of 10 are easy: $10^5=100{,}000$, which is a 1 followed by five zeros. Any number except zero raised to the power 0 is 1, so $5^0=1$. An exponent of 1 changes nothing: $7^1=7$.

learn.title: Negative bases
learn.body: The sign of $(-2)^3$ and $(-2)^2$ depends on how many negatives you multiply.
steps: Compare $(-2)^2=4$: an even exponent gives a positive result.

learn.body: Without brackets, the exponent only applies to what it touches. $-2^2$ means $-(2^2)=-4$, but $(-2)^2=4$.

questions.prompt: In $5^2$, the number 5 is called the \_\_.
questions.explanation: The base is the number being multiplied. The exponent (2) says how many times to use it.
$10^5$ is a 1 followed by five zeros: 100000.
Three negative factors give a negative result: $(-2)\times(-2)\times(-2)=-8$.
The exponent applies only to 2, so $-2^2=-(2\times 2)=-4$.

questions.prompt: Match each power with its value.
questions.explanation: $4\times4\times4=64$, $7\times 7=49$, and any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.
